Before I write it up, one thing I haven't asked yet: **what's prompting the guide now, and what would make it a success for the museum?**

The answer decides what the design treats as essential and what it leaves out. Some examples of what it could change: how much a visitor's phone has to do, whether the museum needs to know which stories get played, and how much effort is worth putting into the Welsh side.

After that, I'll set out a choice about how to build it before writing anything. Your website is static pages rebuilt on each deploy, so it has no place to accept a volunteer's upload. Volunteers need somewhere to send a recording that then gets cleaned up and published without anyone technical stepping in. There are a few real ways to do that, and they differ in cost and in what volunteers would see. I'll lay those out with my pick.

On size, this is a project rather than a small change. It will become a full written design that someone could build from. A reviewer will read the design before you see it, and I may come back once with a few questions from that review.
